62 of 97 Survived the Hindenburg. Where.caption:
62 of 97 Survived the Hindenburg. Where You Stood Decided Who Lived.

Ninety-seven people were on the Hindenburg when it burned. Sixty-two survived. The difference was where they happened to be standing.

She Threw Her Sons Out of the Hindenburg.caption:
She Threw Her Sons Out of the Hindenburg Window. Then She Jumped.

When the Hindenburg sank toward the ground, Matilde Doehner threw her two young sons out of the dining-room window, then jumped after them. All three lived.

80,000 People. Fewer Than 10 Died. A 100.caption:
80,000 People. Fewer Than 10 Died. A 100-Year-Old Story Saved Them.

When the 2004 tsunami hit Simeulue, an island right next to the epicentre, almost everyone ran to the hills. They had learned why from a story called smong, told to children since a tsunami in 1907.

A 10-Year-Old Saw the Sea Pull Back and Knew a Tsunami Was Coming

On Mai Khao beach in Phuket, 10-year-old Tilly Smith recognised the warning signs from a geography lesson two weeks earlier. Her parents warned the beach and the hotel staff. No one on that beach was killed.
